name: Shapewear and Seamless
summary: Smooth, bone-free underwear of stretch nylon and elastane: control-top tights, high-waist briefs and bodysuits. They are made seamless or with bonded edges, so that they hold the body and show no line under the dress.

philosophy.core_thesis: Shaping can be soft: a knit with elastane holds the body without bone and leaves no line under the cloth.
design_principles: Knit the body from nylon and elastane, with 15 to 40 per cent elastane for firm hold.
Knit the garment in the round, or bond the edges, so that no seam shows.
Use zones: firm powernet at the stomach and the thigh, and a lighter knit elsewhere.
Raise the waist to the natural waist, and lengthen the leg to the mid-thigh.
Cut the edge with a laser or a bonded band, so that it lies flat on the skin.
Match the cloth to a wide range of skin tones, in at least 10 shades.
Leave out the bone, the busk and the metal hook.
anti_patterns: A visible seam or ridge under the dress
A thick band that digs into the skin

silhouette.shape: A smooth, continuous body line: a flat stomach, a rounded hip and a defined waist, with no edge in view.
silhouette.line: One long line from the waist to the thigh; the edge lies flat.
silhouette.fit: Close and firm in the zones that hold, light and open at the rest; the cloth stretches and recovers.
silhouette.proportion: Waist at the natural waist; leg to mid-thigh or to the knee; band 3 to 5 cm; garment 120 to 260 g/m².
rules: Knit the garment in zones of different hold.
Bond or laser-cut each edge so that it lies flat.
Raise the waist to the natural waist for a smooth stomach.
Lengthen the leg so that the thigh has no roll at the edge.
Offer the colour in a range of skin tones.

fabrics.rule: Use nylon and elastane knits in zones of different hold, with no bone and no metal.

methods: zones of powernet at the stomach
construction.closures: No closure on a pull-on garment; a hook-and-eye or a snap at the crotch on a bodysuit.
construction.details: A bonded edge, a cotton gusset, a wide waistband, a small label at the back, and a zone of firm net.

surface.pattern: Plain skin tones, black and white; no print on the part that shapes.
surface.gloss: Matte at 3–8 GU; sheer nylon at 15–30 GU.
surface.wear: The elastane relaxes after 50 or more washes, and the cloth pills at the edge.

palette.strategy: A wide range of skin tones, with black and white; the aim is the line that does not show.

processes: yarn of nylon covered with elastane
seamless knit on a circular machine
zones of powernet knitted in the body
heat set to fix the shape
making.scale: Made in a factory on seamless machines in large lots. A mill made the first control-top tights of 2000 after a founder in Atlanta persuaded it to run a trial.
making.signs: No side seam, a bonded edge, zones of firm net, a wide waistband, and a range of skin tones.

emotion.target_response: A sense of ease and a smooth line: the garment does its work and no one sees it.

a technical specification of a knit

avoid_when: the brief wants a boned corset
the brief wants a period reconstruction

modifiers.how: Add a steel busk, bone and a laced back; drop the seamless knit.
Choose a bold colour and a satin, and wear the bodysuit as a top with a jacket.

ornament_level.note: The style is plain; a small print or lace edge is the limit.
